---
title: "Stage 5 – The exercise"
aliases:
  - /tracks/self-study/stage-5.html
---
The five tasks were written to be worked through in a class, and they hold up alone with one adjustment: nothing is timed, so take the reproduction in Task 3 as slowly as it needs. The browser lab contains the whole exercise on one page. The reproduction in Task 3 has two hints and a fully worked solution behind collapsible callouts, and the three gaps in Task 5 share one hint, which gives the model syntax for the reproduced specification, the one that the preregistration block holds before you change any of its choices.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) | Re-read the task-by-task section now that you have worked through the modules, and use it as a guide to the rows below. | 20 minutes |
| Your workspace, or the [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) | Tasks 1 to 3: run the setup check and confirm that the panel has 270 rows; meet the panel, write the estimand and finish the causal graph; then fit the constrained model and reproduce **t = −3.804**, the value recorded by Multi100 for analyst C6HJR. | 90 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd) | Read the fourteen decisions, the three levels into which they sort, the options that the curve of 864 keeps and the claim-alignment convention before you touch Task 4, so that 'supports the claim' means the same thing on every axis. | 30 minutes |
| [Decision map](../../cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) | Work through every decision of an analysis of the claim in the order in which an analyst meets it, select options on the curve and off it, and read how each rewrites the estimand statement and what it does to the results, before you choose yours. | 20 minutes |
| Task 4, in the workspace or on the [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-explore) | Try three or four specifications with `try_spec()`, print them side by side with `my_experiments()`, then decide which one you would defend, run it once more so it is the most recent call, and submit it with `submit_exploration()`, which sends the last specification you tried, whatever else is in the log. | 45 minutes |
| Task 5, in the workspace or on the [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-5-my-preregistration) | Complete the preregistration block and run `prereg()` **before** writing any model code. Then translate the specification in the block into model syntax yourself, run it, and submit with `report_result()`. | 45 minutes |
| [Cheatsheet](../../cases/eu-frames/cheatsheet.qmd) | Keep it open while you work. If the browser lab stalls, the first two of the four steps listed there are the ones you can take alone. Steps 3 and 4 and the by-hand lookup assume a facilitator you do not have. | as needed |

**The class chart when working alone.** Submitting works as it does in a taught session. Both `submit_exploration()` and `report_result()` print a pre-filled form link, and pressing Send puts your dot on the [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd) page. What is missing is the comparison around which the day is built, with the dots of a whole class arriving on one chart within a few minutes of each other. The upper chart on that page is pre-computed and always complete, showing the 864 specifications of the curve of the claim with the five Multi100 reanalyses and the published coefficient of the original author (OA) tagged on it. The live chart at the foot of the page fetches whatever submissions have arrived and redraws when you press *Run Code*, and between deliveries there may be very few of them, or none at all. So read the comparisons you can actually make. Your placement among the 864 specifications, the share of them that lie further in the direction of the claim than your result, which `try_spec()` and `run_spec()` print beside your coefficient, can be read against the six tagged results, whose placements run from about 17% for KEVF1 to about 96% for 018OL, as the table of reference marks on the [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#reference-marks) page shows. And `my_experiments()` prints the small multiverse that you built yourself, which stands in, on a small scale, for the spread of results that a class would produce.

**By the end of the stage** you have reproduced **t = −3.804** yourself and completed the preregistration block before running the analysis that it fixes. The [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd) page carries two dots of your own, one from the exploration in Task 4 and one from the specification preregistered in Task 5.
